newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish ship sinks in Bosphorus collision.
newsitem.headline: Turkish ship sinks in Bosphorus collision.

text.p: A Turkish ship sank on Sunday after a collision in heavy fog in Istanbul's Bosphorus strait that killed one crew member, port officials and Turkish media said.
The Maltese-registered, Maria-1 freighter and the Turkish coaster vessel Celiktrans, carrying sand, collided near the northern entrance to the strait, a port official told Reuters.
Anatolian news agency said a crew member from the Turkish ship died and another was injured.
The strait was later closed to further traffic due to the fog, which impeded rescue efforts, port officials said.
The 19-mile-long Bosphorus, a busy waterway key to shipping traffic between the Mediterranean and Black Seas, passes directly through Istanbul and is only 700 metres (yards) wide in places.
The Montreux Convention of 1936 which governs shipping in the strait does not require ships' captains to use a pilot through the waterway.
About 45,000 vessels a year pass through the strait. About 60 percent of them carry oil or oil derivatives, natural gas, chemicals and nuclear waste.
